**Step 1 — Scene:** A plate of whole almonds alongside a small spinach salad with shredded carrot.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A rounded-square plate, approximately 23 cm across. Using an equivalent circular diameter of about 25 cm gives an area of **3.14 × 12.5² ≈ 491 cm²**.

**Steps 3–6 — Items, coverage, volume and weight:**

| Item | Plate area covered | Area × typical height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Whole almonds | 25% | 123 cm² × 1.0 cm = 123 ml | 0.58 g/ml | 71 g |
| Spinach leaves | 34% | 167 cm² × 1.6 cm = 267 ml | 0.15 g/ml | 40 g |
| Shredded carrot | 2% | 10 cm² × 0.6 cm = 6 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 4 g |
| Light oily dressing, inferred from sheen | Overlaps salad | Thin coating, approximately 4 ml | 1.0 g/ml | 4 g |

Food covers approximately **61% of the plate**. Dressing overlaps the leaves rather than adding separate coverage.

**Step 7 — Energy:** Almonds: 71 g × 579 kcal/100 g ≈ 411 kcal; spinach: 40 g × 23 ≈ 9 kcal; carrot: 4 g × 41 ≈ 2 kcal; estimated oil-based dressing: 4 g × 884 ≈ 35 kcal.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **119 g and 457 kcal** is plausible: the leafy salad weighs little, while the substantial almond pile contributes almost all the energy. Dressing quantity is particularly uncertain.
